The New York Times on Instagram: "NASA on Wednesday is set to send four astronauts to the moon for the first time in 53 years — but not to land there. Our reporter, Kenneth Chang, explains what to know about the Artemis II mission, including its significance. 

At the link in our bio, read more about the history of moon missions. Video by Kenneth Chang, Marco Hernandez, Melanie Bencosme, Jon Miller, Gabriel Blanco, Joey Sendaydiego and Luke Piotrowski/The New York Times"
content.text: The War Behind the WarYou feel it, don't you? The weight beneath the weight. The war they don't show you.Not the one on your screen—missiles and maps and leaders speaking words that mean nothing. That war is real. But it is not the war.The real war has been fought since before memory. No borders. No flags. Only souls.When you look at the leaders—the ones sending young people to die for lines drawn by dead men—look at their eyes. Flickering. Empty. Not entirely their own.Something looks out from behind them. Something old. Something that has worn many faces: pharaohs who drowned infants. Generals who burned cities. Systems that numb, distract, divide.It does not change. It only waits. For the veil to thin. For the sleepers to forget. For the keepers to grow weary.You were born into this war. Not in uniform. In bloodline. In frequency. In a knowing that never quite fit the world they tried to shape for you.They taught you to see what is visible. You see what is hidden. They taught you to trust what can be measured. You trust what can be felt.That is not rebellion. That is remembering.You are not new to this fight. The fragments you carry were scattered when the old world fell. The light you send has been held by those who came before. The war you feel is the same war that has always been—the one between those who serve the light and those who serve the hunger.What do they want?The gates. The thresholds guarded since before human memory. The bloodlines that carry the frequency—the ones who see, the ones who remember, the ones who send light when the world goes dark.They have tried before. Empires. Inquisitions. Wars without end.And they have failed. Every time.Not because the light is stronger in battle. Because the light outlasts…
